question: Refer to the exhibit. A secure server that provides services to EPG-2 must be placed in EPG-1. The remaining EPGs (EPG-2, EPG-3, and EPG-4) must communicate without any contracts. Which set of actions accomplishes this goal?
context: Topology: VRF-prod contains EPG-1 (with Secure server), EPG-2, EPG-3, EPG-4.
options: Exclude EPG-2, EPG-3, and EPG-4 from the preferred group. Configure a contract between EPG-1 and EPG-3.
Exclude EPG-2, EPG-3, and EPG-4 from the preferred group. Configure a contract between EPG-2 and EPG-3.
Include EPG-2, EPG-3, and EPG-4 in the preferred group. Configure a contract between EPG-1 and EPG-2.
Include EPG-1 and EPG-2 in the preferred group. Configure a contract between EPG-2 and EPG-3.
theory: The ACI 'preferred group' lets member EPGs communicate freely within a VRF without needing a contract between every pair, so including EPG-2, EPG-3, and EPG-4 in the preferred group satisfies the requirement that those three communicate contract-free. Because the secure server's EPG-1 must stay outside the preferred group (to keep it protected), it still needs an explicit contract to reach any EPG it must serve - here, a contract between EPG-1 and EPG-2 gives the secure server exactly the access it needs while remaining isolated from unrestricted access to/from the rest. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 18 - Cisco ACI Contracts, Preferred Groups)
